memory_update.text: LOPE is the reference public pure-play for university services and online/hybrid program execution; use it as the benchmark for partner-count, service-revenue and enrollment-support metrics.
GHC/Kaplan is a high-priority underfollowed candidate because the OPM-style exposure is hidden inside a diversified holding company and tied to a long-duration Purdue Global support agreement.
NNI is not a direct OPM, but its education technology and payments segment may represent an adjacent institutional back-office chokepoint worth testing in later layers.
COUR is a speculative-shadow candidate for universities shifting from full-service OPM arrangements toward platform distribution, degrees, certificates and employer-linked credentials.
Private OPMs such as Risepoint/Academic Partnerships appear important to the node but are not US-listed; track as private competitive context rather than public-market candidates.

2U/edX historically anchored the OPM reference set, but current public-market eligibility must be checked carefully because restructuring/delisting history may make it unsuitable for the US-listed universe.

node: University services and online program management
summary: Expanded the universe for the university-services/OPM node with a two-lane funnel. The reference anchor is Grand Canyon Education because it is the cleanest public pure-play service provider to university partners. The underfollowed lane adds Graham Holdings/Kaplan, Nelnet, and Coursera: each is one step away from the obvious OPM screen via Purdue Global support services, education payments/back-office systems, or university-backed degree/course distribution. The key chokepoint hypothesis remains institutional trust plus execution capability, but several candidates need later-layer verification on contract durability, partner concentration, regulatory exposure, and whether university services are material enough to drive equity value.
